subject: physics
question: Explain velocity time graphs for JEE using this example: a car speeds up from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s, then moves at a steady 20 m/s until t = 10 s. How do slope and area give acceleration and distance?

qualitativeClaims.claim: On a velocity–time graph, the slope (gradient) at any interval equals the acceleration: a = Δv/Δt.
From t = 0 to 4 s the graph is a straight line rising from (0, 0) to (4, 20); its slope is +5 m/s², so the car has constant acceleration of 5 m/s².
From t = 4 s to 10 s the graph is horizontal at v = 20 m/s; zero slope means zero acceleration (uniform velocity).
The area under a velocity–time graph over an interval equals the displacement (distance, since motion is in one direction with positive velocity).
qualitativeClaims.expected: d = ∫v dt = area under v–t curve

qualitativeClaims.claim: Area from 0 to 4 s is a triangle: ½ × base × height = ½ × 4 s × 20 m/s = 40 m.
Area from 4 s to 10 s is a rectangle: 6 s × 20 m/s = 120 m.
Total distance travelled in 10 s is the sum of the two areas: 40 m + 120 m = 160 m.
JEE tip: a curved v–t graph means non-uniform acceleration (slope changes point to point), and area below the time axis counts as negative displacement.
qualitativeClaims.expected: sign of area = sign of displacement; slope sign = acceleration direction

lawIds: kinematics: acceleration as time derivative of velocity (a = dv/dt)
kinematics: displacement as integral of velocity (d = ∫v dt)
geometry: area of triangle and rectangle
assumptions: Motion is along a straight line in one direction, so distance equals magnitude of displacement.
Acceleration is constant during 0–4 s (straight-line graph).
Velocity remains exactly 20 m/s during 4–10 s.
